task.description:
Resolve ISS-0210. `GIT_MERGE.md` step 5 rebases the feature branch onto `origin/main`. Step 6 then says plainly `git push origin feature/<run-id>`. `GIT_SETUP.md` step 7 mandates the SAME branch already being pushed at Step 00, as the coordination signal. A rebase rewrites every commit on the branch, so step 6's push is a non-fast-forward EVERY TIME a rebase actually replayed anything -- and step 6 never says so or says what to do about it. `ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 7.1 says, in a different context (ORCH pushing its own registry commits to `main`), "do not force" -- read literally alongside step 6's silence, a run whose branch was rebased has no legal way to publish its own feature branch. This is not hypothetical: `WF03-ISS0200-20260821`'s own Step Final hit it live. ORCH had written an over-broad blanket no-force-push instruction into that run's Step Final dispatch, caught the over-breadth mid-step, and corrected it to authorize `--force-with-lease` on the run's OWN branch specifically while keeping the prohibition on `main` and on any other session's commits. The agent receiving that correction did not even use the authorization -- it reset to the already-published tip and merged `origin/main` into it instead, then proved byte-level equivalence against the discarded rebase tree before proceeding. Read the full findings first-hand in `handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json` `result.issues` -- this dispatch summarizes only enough to size the work; ISS-0210 is ORCH's filing of the same, plus two smaller items from that handoff.

FOUR THINGS TO DO. Steps 1-2 are the load-bearing gap; 3-4 are the two smaller items filed alongside it.

1. RE-DERIVE THE NON-FAST-FORWARD CLAIM FIRST-HAND, don't take it as given. Confirm from the protocol text (`GIT_SETUP.md` step 7, `GIT_MERGE.md` steps 5-6) that the sequence as written guarantees this, and confirm against at least one real run's handoff/log evidence that step 5 followed by step 6 actually produced (or would have produced) a rejected push. `WF03-ISS0200-20260821`'s own Step Final handoff is the primary source; state what it shows.

2. WRITE THE RULE, WITH ITS BOUNDARY, IN GIT_MERGE.md STEP 6. State plainly: after a rebase that replayed any commits, step 6's push targets the run's OWN feature branch and may use `--force-with-lease` (never bare `--force` -- lease checks the remote hasn't moved since your last fetch, which matters exactly when a concurrent session might have pushed to the SAME feature branch, though that should be rare since one branch belongs to one run). State the boundary explicitly and by name: this authorization covers ONLY the run's own `feature/<run-id>` branch. It never extends to `main`, and never to a commit authored by a different session -- `ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 7.1's prohibition on those is UNCHANGED and this ruling does not touch it. If step 5's rebase was a no-op (no commits actually replayed, e.g. the branch was already up to date with `origin/main`), the ordinary `git push` still works and no force is needed -- say so, so the rule isn't read as 'always force'.

3. KEEP THE TWO DOCUMENTS CONSISTENT. The rule belongs in GIT_MERGE.md step 6, since that is the step it gates. `ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 7.1 is about a different actor (ORCH itself) pushing to `main` from a shared checkout, a genuinely different situation -- but confirm it does not ALSO need to be read as covering feature-branch pushes, and if a reader could plausibly conflate the two, add ONE clarifying sentence there that points at GIT_MERGE.md rather than restating the rule. Do not duplicate the rule in both files.

4. THE TWO SMALLER ITEMS, same source handoff. (a) AC4-style byte-identity checks in this project's runs read spans from the WORKING TREE, which `core.autocrlf` rewrites -- the step-final handoff found the same content hashing differently by +1 byte per line right after a rebase, on this host. VERIFY this yourself on this host before writing anything (`git config --get core.autocrlf`, and a small before/after hash comparison across a rebase-equivalent operation) -- do not take the prior run's finding as given. If confirmed, add a short note wherever this project's git-step guidance discusses byte-identity verification (check `GIT_MERGE.md` and `HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` for existing language) stating that such a check must hash the git BLOB (`git show <sha>:<path>` or `git cat-file blob <sha>`), never a working-tree file read. (b) A `.gitattributes` union merge driver for `handoffs/orchestrator.log` and `handoffs/registry.json` is proposed, since both are append-only by protocol and their conflict class is now recurring (this run's own predecessor, WF03-ISS0209, hit exactly this kind of conflict against a concurrent WF03-ISS0200 push). Decide, explicitly, whether to adopt it -- for the `.log` file, a `union` merge driver is a plausible fit (git's built-in `merge=union` unions lines, which is close to what manual resolution does for a linear log). For `registry.json`, the JSON structure means a naive `union` driver could produce syntactically invalid or duplicate-keyed JSON on anything other than a clean append -- state explicitly whether you adopt it for that file too, and why. A NO-CHANGE / not-adopted outcome is legitimate here if the judgement goes that way; state the reasoning either way, per this issue's own AC5.

SCOPE:
- Docs-only. Do not touch `lib/`, `priv/repo/migrations/`, `test/` or `web/`.
- `docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` section 1.2 and its neighboring `git_evidence` subsection are NOT in scope for this run beyond a pointer if item 4a needs one -- ISS-0206 and ISS-0208 may still be open against section 1.2 depending on queue state; check before touching it, and if you must reference the `git_evidence` scope ruling, point at it rather than restating it.
- Close the issue (WF-03 Step 5, taken within this step): `docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml` gets `status: resolved`, `resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0210-20260821`, `resolved_at:` from a real clock read. Close GH#402 naming this run and the issue file.
- `result.status` must be one of PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/SKIPPED.
- Read the clock in its OWN command before each timestamp. Never batch `date -u` with the write that consumes it.
- `started_at` was stamped by ORCH at dispatch. Claim by setting `status` to `IN_PROGRESS` only.
- Commit `docs/` and this handoff. Do NOT write `handoffs/registry.json` or `handoffs/orchestrator.log`.
acceptance_criteria: The non-fast-forward claim is re-derived first-hand from the protocol text and from at least one real run's evidence (WF03-ISS0200-20260821's Step Final handoff), not merely asserted

GIT_MERGE.md step 6 states the permission AND its boundary: --force-with-lease is authorized ONLY on the run's own feature/<run-id> branch, never on main and never on another session's commit; a no-op rebase needing no force is also stated
ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.1 and GIT_MERGE.md are left mutually consistent, with the rule stated in exactly one place and any cross-reference a pointer, not a restatement
The autocrlf finding is verified first-hand on this host before being acted on, and any byte-identity guidance added names the git blob rather than the working tree
An explicit adopt/do-not-adopt decision is recorded for a .gitattributes union merge driver, covering both orchestrator.log and registry.json separately, with reasoning for each
docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml carries status: resolved, resolved_in_run and a clock-read resolved_at; GH#402 is closed
Section 1.2 and any issue still open against it are left untouched beyond a pointer if genuinely needed; no file outside docs/ and handoffs/WF03-ISS0210-20260821/ is modified

result.summary:
ISS-0210 resolved. All four items done, docs-only, no git wrapper (this run edits protocol prose, not a feature branch).

(1) NON-FAST-FORWARD RE-DERIVED FIRST-HAND. From protocol text: GIT_SETUP.md step 7 pushes feature/<run-id> at Step 00 (`git push -u origin feature/<run-id>`); GIT_MERGE.md step 5 then rebases onto origin/main, rewriting every commit made since. Step 6's plain `git push origin feature/<run-id>` therefore targets a remote ref still at the pre-rebase tip whenever the rebase replayed anything -- a non-fast-forward by construction, not by chance. From real evidence: handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json result.issues[0] confirms this was hit live -- that run's dispatch had to be corrected mid-step from a blanket no-force instruction to a scoped --force-with-lease authorization after the branch was rebased twice; the run in fact never exercised the authorization (it reset to the published tip and merged origin/main instead, then proved tree equivalence), but the deadlock the gap creates is real and is exactly what the correction was needed for.

(2)+(3) GIT_MERGE.md step 6 now states: try the plain push first (a no-op rebase needs no force and the ordinary push succeeds); on an actual non-fast-forward rejection, --force-with-lease (never bare --force) republishes the run's OWN feature/<run-id> branch, because the lease check protects against the one case that would matter -- a concurrent session pushing the same branch. The boundary is stated by name: never main, never another session's commit, ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1's prohibition on those is unchanged. ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1 (the 'do not force' line, about ORCH pushing shared registry/log commits to main from a checkout other ORCH-role sessions may share) gained exactly one pointer sentence to GIT_MERGE.md step 6, distinguishing the two cases rather than restating the rule -- it lives in exactly one place.

(4a) autocrlf verified first-hand on this host, not taken as given: `git config --get core.autocrlf` -> `true` (set at the system gitconfig level, C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig). Demonstrated live rather than simulated: `git show HEAD:docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md | sha256sum` differs from `sha256sum` of the checked-out working-tree copy of the same file right now (67b0baae... vs c61bbace...), and a hex dump of the working-tree file's first bytes shows 0d0a (CRLF) where the committed blob has LF -- confirming the CRLF rewrite is live on this host for a currently-tracked .md file, the same class ISS-0200 hit on protected spans after a rebase. Root cause: .gitattributes forces `eol=lf` only for *.ex/*.exs (ISS-0008), leaving .md/.json checked out under the host's ambient core.autocrlf. Added a note in GIT_MERGE.md's conflict-handling section (step 5b area) requiring byte-identity checks to hash the git blob (`git show <sha>:<path>` / `git cat-file blob <sha>`), never the working-tree file.

(4b) .gitattributes union-driver decision, made separately per file: ADOPTED `merge=union` for handoffs/orchestrator.log -- it is a flat append-only line log, and git's built-in union driver (unions lines, drops exact duplicates) matches the outcome hand-resolution already produces there (WF03-ISS0200-20260821's own evidence: line count only grew, origin/main's lines an exact prefix of the resolved file). NOT ADOPTED for handoffs/registry.json -- it is JSON, and a naive line union has no structural awareness: two sessions each appending one entry commonly touch the SAME closing `}`/`]` lines, and a line union over that can produce invalid or duplicate-keyed JSON, which this file cannot tolerate since every run depends on it parsing. Hand-resolution stays mandatory there per ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1; reasoning for both recorded in .gitattributes itself, not just here.

Section 1.2 (ISS-0206, ISS-0208, both still open) was not touched beyond confirming neither issue's scope overlaps this one -- no pointer to it was needed since item 4a's guidance landed in GIT_MERGE.md, not HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (no existing byte-identity language was found there to extend; the one 'byte-identical' hit in that file is about a completed_at timestamp match, unrelated).

ISS-0210 closed: docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml carries status: resolved, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0210-20260821, resolved_at from a clock read taken in its own command. GH#402 closed via `gh issue close 402` with a comment naming this run and the issue file.
